meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'well; come on', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'what', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'this', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to leave, go away', paired with 'уходить'.
High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and, but; so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'yes, indeed', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'this, that; it is', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'to you', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?
And this is for you. A toy car!

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronominal determiner meaning 'my, mine', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('former, ex-').

examples.text: Мне нужно немножко поработать с бывшим мэром.
examples.trans: I need to do a little work on the former mayor.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian clause-linking conjunction meaning 'and', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

давно.gloss: for a long time; long ago

meanings.en: for a long time; long ago
meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: You haven't been interested in me for a long time.

examples.text: Вспомнил? Я давно тебя не интересую.
examples.trans: Now you remember? You haven't been interested in me for a long time.

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'статься'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to break up, to part', paired with 'расставаться'.

examples.text: Нет, я всё решил! Мы с ней точно расстанемся.
examples.trans: No, I have decided everything! She and I will definitely break up.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'лгода'). Common masculine noun meaning 'half a year, six months' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I've been here for six months now.

examples.text: Ты эти деньги через полгода вернёшь.
examples.trans: You'll get this money back in six months.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'ago; back, backwards', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Я их ещё два года назад им выделил!
examples.trans: I allocated it to them two years ago!

examples.text: Я их ещё два года назад им выделил! Я сам приказ подписывал!
examples.trans: I allocated it to them two years ago! I signed the order myself!

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'no; there isn't', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'пасибо'). Common neuter noun meaning 'thank you' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'in (time); through', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Нормально? Она через неделю снова потечёт!
examples.trans: Fine? It'll be leaking again in a week!

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'деля'). Common feminine noun meaning 'week' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'we', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'говорить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to have a talk', paired with 'говорить'.

examples.text: Поговори с Аракеляном. Пусть он заберёт заявление.
examples.trans: Talk to Arakelyan. Get him to withdraw his statement.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian spatial or relational preposition meaning 'with', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'here is; (emphasis) that's', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'he; it', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'нятый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('busy; occupied, taken').
Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'ождать'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'wait', paired with 'ждать'.

examples.text: Подожди, Нин, ты не поняла. Это же стыдно!
examples.trans: Wait, Nina, you don't get it. It's shameful!
Wait, where are you two going?

examples.text: Подождите! Два дня — это же очень мало.
examples.trans: Hold on! Two days is far too little.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'here', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'жалуйста').
High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'now', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Теперь я начальник нашей стройки. Ты уволен!
examples.trans: Now I'm the boss of our building site. You're fired!

examples.text: Ну что, довольна? Теперь новую работу искать.
examples.trans: Well, happy now? Now I have to look for a new job.
Now I have to look for a new job.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be jealous of'.

related.gloss: to be jealous for a while

examples.trans: Are you jealous of my past?
Max, tell the truth, are you jealous?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'I', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.
